**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**

COLUMBUS, Ohio — A coordinated investigation spanning three states led to the arrest Tuesday of a 34-year-old Indiana man accused of using social media to groom and eventually transport a 14-year-old Ohio girl across state lines, according to authorities from the FBI's Cincinnati Field Office and local law enforcement agencies.

Marcus D. Whitfield of Fort Wayne, Indiana, was taken into custody without incident at a motel in Louisville, Kentucky, following a joint operation involving the FBI's Innocent Images task force, the Ohio Bureau of Criminal Investigation, Indiana State Police, and Louisville Metro Police.

According to court documents, Whitfield allegedly first made contact with the victim through an Instagram account roughly four months ago, posing as a 17-year-old. Investigators say the communication escalated over several weeks through direct messages and a third-party messaging app before moving to encrypted platforms.

The girl was reported missing by her family from her home in Dayton, Ohio, on Saturday. Local detectives immediately began working with the FBI's Child Exploitation Task Force, which had flagged similar online activity connected to Whitfield in an unrelated case originating in Michigan earlier this year.

"This is exactly why interagency cooperation matters," said Special Agent in Charge Rebecca Torres of the FBI Cincinnati office. "Predators don't respect state lines, and neither can we in how we respond. The moment Ohio authorities entered information into our shared database, we were able to cross-reference it with intelligence already being developed in two other jurisdictions."

Investigators used cell-tower data and information obtained through a search warrant served on the social media company to track the pair's movement from Dayton through Cincinnati and into Kentucky. Louisville police, alerted by federal partners, located the vehicle at a motel off Interstate 65 and set up surveillance before making the arrest.

The victim was found safe and has been reunited with her family. She is receiving support services through a regional child advocacy center, officials said.

Whitfield faces federal charges including coercion and enticement of a minor and transportation of a minor with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity, both of which carry mandatory minimum sentences upon conviction. He is also expected to face state charges in Ohio.

"These cases move fast, and they don't stay within one county or one state," said Dayton Police Chief Elaine Marsh. "The only reason we recovered this child within 72 hours is because agencies picked up the phone immediately instead of waiting on paperwork."

Authorities said Whitfield has no prior criminal record in Indiana but noted that the investigation remains ongoing, with agents reviewing his electronic devices for evidence of contact with other potential victims.

The FBI is asking anyone with information related to the case, or who may have had contact with an account under the name "Marcus_W_34" or similar aliases, to contact the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children or their local FBI field office.

Whitfield is being held without bond pending an initial federal court appearance in the Western District of Kentucky.
